sentences.en: Um, it's called a ternary search tree.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它叫三叉搜索树（ternary search tree）。

sentences.en: Um, this is something I first came across, uh, when I was working on Boost Spirit towards the start of my career.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我在职业生涯初期研究 Boost Spirit 时第一次接触到的。

sentences.en: For those who don't know, Boost Spirit is, um, uh, a C++, um, uh, parsing framework.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的人，Boost Spirit 是，嗯，呃，一个 C++，嗯，呃，解析框架。

sentences.en: Um, it's sort of a, it's an alternative to something like Yak and Bison, um, uh, which are, uh, uh, uh, two common, uh, parser frameworks for, uh, uh, like C or C++.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它算是一种，它是像 Yacc 和 Bison 之类的替代品，嗯，呃，它们是，呃，呃，呃，两种常见的，呃，解析器框架，用于，呃，呃，比如 C 或 C++。

sentences.en: But the advantage of Boost Spirit is that it does not require some external tool to generate your, uh, parser.
sentences.zh: 但 Boost Spirit 的优势在于它不需要任何外部工具来生成你的，呃，解析器。

sentences.en: Um, it's all done in C++ using a domain-specific embedded language and, uh, C++ expression templates.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它完全是用 C++ 完成的，使用了领域特定嵌入式语言和，呃，C++ 表达式模板。

sentences.en: Um, and so one of the things that, uh, uh, we, um, have as part of Boost Spirit is, um, there's this primitive, um, that's called, uh, uh, symbols.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们在 Boost Spirit 中拥有的东西之一是，嗯，有一个原语，嗯，叫做，呃，呃，符号（symbols）。

sentences.en: And that's for storing, like, um, you know, a set of keywords, um, or something like that.
sentences.zh: 那是用来存储，比如，嗯，你知道，一组关键字，嗯，或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: Um, some set of, uh, uh, of known, um, strings that you want to match againSt. And, um, we use a ternary search tree, um, um, uh, to store these symbols tables.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一些已知的，呃，呃，字符串集合，你想用来进行匹配。而且，嗯，我们使用三叉搜索树，嗯，嗯，呃，来存储这些符号表。

sentences.en: Um, and a ternary search tree, it's a special type of, um, try.
sentences.zh: 嗯，三叉搜索树，它是，嗯，字典树（trie）的一种特殊类型。

sentences.en: Um, so each node has a value.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以每个节点都有一个值。

sentences.en: In, in our case, the value is just going to be a character.
sentences.zh: 在，在我们的例子中，这个值就是一个字符。

sentences.en: Um, and then three children.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后有三个子节点。

sentences.en: Um, and one of those children is the low child.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一个子节点是较小（low）子节点。

sentences.en: Um, and you go down that branch if the value that you're searching for is less than the node's value.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你要搜索的值小于节点的值，你就沿着那个分支向下走。

sentences.en: Then you have an equal child, um, and you go down that branch if the value that you're searching for is equal to the node's value.
sentences.zh: 然后你有一个相等（equal）子节点，嗯，如果你要搜索的值等于节点的值，你就沿着那个分支向下走。

sentences.en: And then you have a greater child and you go down that one if the value you're searching for is greater than the node's value.
sentences.zh: 然后你有一个较大（greater）子节点，如果你要搜索的值大于节点的值，你就沿着那个分支走。

sentences.en: Um, and And so because it's a try, it's very nice and space efficient.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为它是字典树，所以它非常简洁且空间效率很高。

sentences.en: For search, insertion, and deletion, it's, I think, O log N average and O N worSt.
sentences.zh: 对于搜索、插入和删除，我认为，平均时间复杂度是 O(log N)，最坏情况是 O(N)。

sentences.en: And you might wonder, well, shouldn't we just use a hash map for something like this?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，嗯，我们不应该直接用哈希映射（hash map）来做这种事吗？

sentences.en: And in a lot of cases, a hash map might be faster.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，哈希映射可能更快。

sentences.en: But in this particular case of Boost Spirits use case, a ternary search tree or a TST, as they're abbreviated to, is a little bit of a better fit.
sentences.zh: 但在 Boost Spirit 的这个特定用例中，三叉搜索树（简称 TST）更合适一些。

sentences.en: So one of the reasons is because a TST search can be done incrementally.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是 TST 搜索可以增量进行。

sentences.en: We can take some sequence of inputs and sort of incrementally search down the tree for them.
sentences.zh: 我们可以获取一系列输入，并以增量方式在树中向下搜索它们。

sentences.en: And this is a really good fit when we're working with iterators, which is what Boost Spirit deals in for input.
sentences.zh: 当我们处理迭代器时，这非常契合，而 Boost Spirit 正是处理迭代器输入的。

sentences.en: Another nice property of TSTs is that mismatches are discovered earlier.
sentences.zh: TST 的另一个优点是失配（mismatch）可以更早被发现。

sentences.en: So in a hash table, a mismatch or a failure to find something, you know, hey, I'm looking in this hash table to see if this symbol is in there.
sentences.zh: 在哈希表中，失配或找不到东西，你知道，嘿，我在这个哈希表中查找这个符号是否存在。

sentences.en: Those can be quite expensive in hash tables.
sentences.zh: 这些在哈希表中可能相当昂贵。

sentences.en: Whereas with a TST, you can get a false answer very quickly.
sentences.zh: 而使用 TST，你可以非常快地得到否定的答案。

sentences.en: Imagine that you had a symbols table where you had no symbols that started with the letter X.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你有一个符号表，里面没有任何以字母 X 开头的符号。

sentences.en: So then if you've got some input that starts with the letter X, you immediately know on the first node that you search that you're done.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你输入的某些内容以字母 X 开头，你在搜索的第一个节点上就会立即知道你完成了。

sentences.en: Because you go to the first node, you see that it's not an X, you go to whichever is the applicable child, and you see that it's a null node.
sentences.zh: 因为你转到第一个节点，看到它不是 X，你转到相应的子节点，发现它是一个空节点。

sentences.en: And you immediately know, hey, there are no symbols in this symbol table that start with the letter X.
sentences.zh: 你立即就知道，嘿，这个符号表中没有以字母 X 开头的符号。

sentences.en: So I know that there's no matches, and I should go on to try to match the next component in the parser.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道没有匹配项，我应该继续尝试匹配解析器中的下一个组件。

sentences.en: And TSTs are also nice because they can provide partial results and nearest neighbors.
sentences.zh: 而且 TST 也很不错，因为它们可以提供部分结果和最近邻。

sentences.en: And so that's useful if, for example, you want to provide some diagnostic if there's a typo.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有用，例如，如果你想在有拼写错误时提供一些诊断信息。

sentences.en: You know, if somebody misspelled a keyword by one letter, a TST can give you some, you know, some close matches.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有人把关键字拼错了一个字母，TST 可以给你一些，你知道，一些接近的匹配项。

sentences.en: And TSTs also, you know, they use less memory, so they're more space efficient.
sentences.zh: 而且 TST，你知道，它们使用的内存更少，所以空间效率更高。

sentences.en: And they can also be more compute efficient because a compact data structure is going to be more cache friendly.
sentences.zh: 它们还可以更具计算效率，因为紧凑的数据结构对缓存更友好。

sentences.en: And you can use TSTs, you see them in a lot of places.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用 TST，你在很多地方都能看到它们。

sentences.en: They're used for things like spell check or auto completion.
sentences.zh: 它们被用于拼写检查或自动补全之类的功能。

sentences.en: They're used a lot in IDEs and text editors and in parser frameworks like Boost Spirit.
sentences.zh: 它们在 IDE、文本编辑器以及像 Boost Spirit 这样的解析框架中被大量使用。

sentences.en: So in the case of Boost Spirit, you said that each of the characters in your TST sort of is one character of a symbol.
sentences.zh: 所以在 Boost Spirit 的例子中，你说 TST 中的每个字符，某种程度上是一个符号的一个字符。

sentences.en: What's an example of, like, the set of symbols that are being stored in this, if I understood correctly?
sentences.zh: 如果我理解正确的话，这里存储的符号集有什么例子吗？

sentences.en: Like, what's an example?
sentences.zh: 比如，有什么例子？

sentences.en: Is it, like, keywords and identifiers from, like, a programming language or some DSL or something like that?
sentences.zh: 是像编程语言中的关键字和标识符，还是某种 DSL 之类的东西？

sentences.en: Yeah, it would be something like keywords or identifiers or, you know, it might be something that you use for, so normally the symbol table is used to map.
sentences.zh: 是的，会是像关键字或标识符之类的东西，或者，你知道，它可能是你用来，所以通常符号表是用来映射的。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily something that you use for keywords, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实不一定是你用来做关键字的东西。

sentences.en: You might, but a better example might be something like built-in functions because the symbol table will map some strings to some values.
sentences.zh: 你可能会用，但更好的例子可能是内置函数之类的东西，因为符号表会将一些字符串映射到一些值。

sentences.en: So, like, let's say that you had some little language that had some built-in, like, names for different colors.
sentences.zh: 所以，假设你有一种小语言，它有一些内置的，比如，不同颜色的名称。

sentences.en: Like, it was some graphics programming language.
sentences.zh: 比如，它是一种图形编程语言。

sentences.en: You might have a symbol table that maps all those names for colors to an object that represents that color.
sentences.zh: 你可能有一个符号表，将所有这些颜色名称映射到一个代表该颜色的对象。

sentences.en: Or if you have a set of built-in functions, like, you know, a set of built-in math functions,
sentences.zh: 或者如果你有一组内置函数，比如，你知道，一组内置数学函数，

sentences.en: you might have a symbol table that maps all the names of those math functions to, you know, a function object that implements those semantics.
sentences.zh: 你可能有一个符号表，将所有这些数学函数的名称映射到，你知道，一个实现这些语义的函数对象。

sentences.en: Although, in that case, you might do it slightly differently in Boost Spirit.
sentences.zh: 虽然在这种情况下，你在 Boost Spirit 中可能会做得略有不同。

sentences.en: But it's generally, it's used for any time where you've got some sort of enumeration or some large set of things that you want to map to some value.
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，它用于任何你有某种枚举或大量你想映射到某个值的对象的情况。

sentences.en: Whereas something like a keyword, you probably would handle a little bit differently because each keyword may appear in a different context in a programming language.
sentences.zh: 而像关键字这样的东西，你可能会以稍微不同的方式处理，因为每个关键字在编程语言中可能出现在不同的上下文中。

sentences.en: Whereas a symbol table in Boost Spirit is something that you're going to use in a place where, hey, any one of these sets of things could appear.
sentences.zh: 而 Boost Spirit 中的符号表是你会在任何这些集合中的任何一个可能出现的地方使用的东西。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Have you ever used Boost Spirit or you've just worked on it from, like, an implementer side of things?
sentences.zh: 你用过 Boost Spirit 吗，还是你只是从实现者的角度参与过？

sentences.en: We used it in HPX, this parallel runtime that I worked on to implement our, like, YAML metadata parser and to implement our command line option parsers.
sentences.zh: 我们在 HPX 中使用了它，这是我工作的一个并行运行时，用来实现我们的，比如 YAML 元数据解析器和命令行选项解析器。

sentences.en: You know, any time that I need to do some parsing in C++ where I can't get away with regular expressions, I'd pick up something like Boost Spirit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何时候我需要在 C++ 中进行解析，而正则表达式无法解决时，我就会选择像 Boost Spirit 这样的东西。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Is it still a recommended library these days?
sentences.zh: 现在它还是一个推荐的库吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: At least in my book.
sentences.zh: 至少在我看来是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, there are some people who are not a fan of it because it does rely very heavily on C++ templates and expression templates.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有些人不喜欢它，因为它非常依赖 C++ 模板和表达式模板。

sentences.en: But I think it's really amazing technology.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这真的是了不起的技术。

sentences.en: It gives you really fast, optimized code at runtime.
sentences.zh: 它在运行时为你提供了非常快速、优化的代码。

sentences.en: And these days, it's very fast to compile, too, especially relative to sort of pre-C++11 compile times, which could be quite painful for these large template code bases.

sentences.en: Oh, there's another place where TSTs are quite useful, which is if you're doing something like case-insensitive parsing, they can be a really good fit for that.
sentences.zh: 哦，TST 还有一个非常有用的地方，就是如果你在做类似不区分大小写的解析，它们非常适合。

sentences.en: Like, hey, I want to match, you know, I want to match these words regardless of whether they're capitalized or lowercase, etc.
sentences.zh: 比如，嘿，我想匹配，你知道，我想匹配这些单词，不管它们是大写还是小写，等等。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 好的，是的，这说得通。

sentences.en: Because the one thing that I'm not entirely clear on is how exactly does a – how does a TST differ from just a regular tree?
sentences.zh: 因为有一点我不完全清楚，就是 TST 与普通树到底有什么不同？

sentences.en: Tri, I guess.
sentences.zh: 字典树（trie），我想是这样。

sentences.en: We're pronouncing it that way.
sentences.zh: 我们是这样发音的。

sentences.en: Well, so it sounded like from your explanation that, like, there's only – there's always a maximum of three children per node.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听你的解释，好像每个节点最多只有三个子节点。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Whereas in a tri or a directed acyclic word graph, basically, like, your boundary is the set of characters.
sentences.zh: 而在字典树或有向无环词图（DAWG）中，基本上，你的边界是字符集。

sentences.en: If so, if it's just, like, alphabetical, Arabic characters, lowercase, that's 26.
sentences.zh: 如果是字母表，阿拉伯字符，小写，那就是 26 个。

sentences.en: But if it's alphanumeric, that's going to be 36.
sentences.zh: 但如果是字母数字，那就是 36 个。

sentences.en: And then if you include whatever, punctuation or capitalize, obviously that increases.
sentences.zh: 如果你包括标点符号或大写，显然会增加。

sentences.en: But so, like, typically for, you know, if you're implementing it for a Scrabble game,
sentences.zh: 所以，比如，通常对于，你知道，如果你在为拼字游戏实现它，

sentences.en: you're going to have a maximum of 26 children node because that's – you don't have to deal with cases and there's no such thing as numbers.
sentences.zh: 你会有最多 26 个子节点，因为那是——你不需要处理大小写，也没有数字之类的东西。

sentences.en: Whereas in your description of a TST, you have, like, the lower bound, the equal node child, and then the upper bound, and that's, like, the max.
sentences.zh: 而在你对 TST 的描述中，你有，比如，较小节点、相等节点子节点，然后是较大节点，这就是最大值。

sentences.en: So, if I understood your explanation correctly.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我正确理解了你的解释的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, no.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，不。

sentences.en: I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: Now, the question is, what are the implications of that tradeoff?
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，这种权衡的含义是什么？

sentences.en: And off the top of my head, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我一时想不出来。

sentences.en: I think we'd have to, like, work through it.
sentences.zh: 我想我们得，比如，研究一下。

sentences.en: Um, is it perhaps the case that one of these two is more space efficient than the other?
sentences.zh: 嗯，会不会是这两者中有一个比另一个更节省空间？

sentences.en: Um, or that searching is quicker in one or the other requires hopping through less – more or less nodes?
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者搜索在其中一个中更快，或者需要跳过更少或更多的节点？

sentences.en: Unfortunately, I have to interrupt episode three because a few minutes later, Bryce would say the following.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我必须打断第三集，因为几分钟后，Bryce 会说以下内容。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: We're going to probably have to cut this part because this is a little bit rambly.
sentences.zh: 我们可能得剪掉这一部分，因为这有点语无伦次。

sentences.en: And due to that statement, it seems that the podcast god smiled down upon Bryce while he was exporting his audio, and they erased the last 20 to 30 minutes of his recording.
sentences.zh: 由于那句话，播客之神似乎在 Bryce 导出音频时对他微笑，他们删除了他录音的最后 20 到 30 分钟。

sentences.en: Fortunately for us, we were going to heavily edit out most of what we were discussing because, uh, clearly at the time,
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们本来就要大量删减我们讨论的大部分内容，因为，呃，显然当时，

sentences.en: we didn't understand how ternary search trees were constructed.
sentences.zh: 我们并不了解三叉搜索树是如何构建的。

sentences.en: Um, unfortunately, what that means is that the edited version of this conversation is just going to be about four to five minutes of my voice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不幸的是，这意味着这个对话的剪辑版本将只有大约四到五分钟我的声音。

sentences.en: So, we apologize for this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对此表示歉意。

sentences.en: Next time, we will make sure that the podcast gods do not interfere, and hopefully this will not happen again.
sentences.zh: 下次，我们会确保播客之神不会干扰，希望这种情况不会再发生。

sentences.en: Back to the episode.
sentences.zh: 回到这一集。

sentences.en: Let's go to the Wikipedia page.
sentences.zh: 让我们去维基百科页面看看。

sentences.en: Ternary search tree is a type of tri, sometimes called a prefix tree, where nodes are arranged in a manner similar to a binary search tree,
sentences.zh: 三叉搜索树是一种字典树，有时被称为前缀树，其中节点的排列方式类似于二叉搜索树，

sentences.en: but with up to three children rather than the binary tree's limit of two.
sentences.zh: 但最多有三个子节点，而不是二叉树的两个限制。

sentences.en: Like other prefix trees, a ternary search tree can be used as an associative map structure with the ability for incremental string search.
sentences.zh: 像其他前缀树一样，三叉搜索树可以用作关联映射结构，具有增量字符串搜索的能力。

sentences.en: However, ternary search trees are more space efficient compared to standard prefix trees at the cost of speed.
sentences.zh: 然而，与标准前缀树相比，三叉搜索树以速度为代价，在空间上更高效。

sentences.en: Common applications for ternary search trees include spellchecking and autocompletion.
sentences.zh: 三叉搜索树的常见应用包括拼写检查和自动补全。

sentences.en: And the description says each node of a ternary search tree stores a single character, an object, or a pointer to an object depending on implementation,
sentences.zh: 描述中说，三叉搜索树的每个节点存储一个字符、一个对象或一个指向对象的指针（取决于实现），

sentences.en: and pointers to its three children conventionally named equal kid, low kid, and high kid, which can also be referred respectively as middle child, lower child, and higher child.
sentences.zh: 以及指向其三个子节点的指针，通常命名为相等子节点、较小子节点和较大子节点，也可以分别称为中间子节点、较小子节点和较大子节点。

sentences.en: If we go on, it says the low kid pointer must point to a node whose character value is less than the current node.
sentences.zh: 继续往下看，它说较小子节点指针必须指向一个字符值小于当前节点的节点。

sentences.en: The high kid pointer must point to a node whose character is greater than the current node.
sentences.zh: 较大子节点指针必须指向一个字符值大于当前节点的节点。

sentences.en: The equal kid points to the next character in the word.
sentences.zh: 相等子节点指向单词中的下一个字符。

sentences.en: The figure below shows a ternary search tree with the strings cute, cup, at, as, he, us, and I.
sentences.zh: 下图显示了一个包含字符串 cute、cup、at、as、he、us 和 I 的三叉搜索树。

sentences.en: Anyway, definitely every leaf node is the end, every leaf node in the TST represents the end of a word.
sentences.zh: 总之，绝对每个叶节点都是结尾，TST 中的每个叶节点都代表一个单词的结尾。

sentences.en: So the left S is for as, the P is for cup, the E is for cute, the I is for just the single letter I,
sentences.zh: 所以左边的 S 是 as，P 是 cup，E 是 cute，I 只是单个字母 I，

sentences.en: the right S is for us, the E on the third level, second from the bottom,
sentences.zh: 右边的 S 是 us，第三层、倒数第二的 E，

sentences.en: is for he.
sentences.zh: 是 he。

sentences.en: And then the only other question is, how does it know that at is a word?
sentences.zh: 那么唯一的问题是，它怎么知道 at 是一个单词？

sentences.en: Because basically there's 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.
So there's seven words.
sentences.zh: 所以有七个单词。

sentences.en: Every single one of those words ends in like a singular leaf node, which is different from the try implementation in the directed acyclic word graph in that.
sentences.zh: 每一个单词都以一个单独的叶节点结束，这与有向无环词图中的字典树实现不同，因为，

sentences.en: Like there's an indicator so that if you have car in cars, car is going to end at the R in C-A-R,
sentences.zh: 比如有一个指示器，所以如果你在 cars 中有 car，car 将在 C-A-R 的 R 处结束，

sentences.en: and you're just going to have like a Boolean indicator flag saying a word ends here.
sentences.zh: 你只会有一个像布尔指示标志的东西，说单词在这里结束。

sentences.en: And it's just like straight from the top node down to that node where it indicates that there's a word.
sentences.zh: 它就像直接从顶部节点向下到那个指示有单词的节点。

sentences.en: And then when you add an S, you're also going to set the flag in that node to like word ending here.
sentences.zh: 然后当你添加一个 S 时，你也会在那个节点中设置标志，比如单词在这里结束。

sentences.en: Whereas here it seems that like a word that starts with a C is going to start from the top, but a word that starts from any other letter is not going to start at that level.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，似乎以 C 开头的单词将从顶部开始，但以任何其他字母开头的单词将不会从该层开始。

sentences.en: Every other letter that's less, you're going to go down to the low node.
sentences.zh: 任何其他较小的字母，你都会向下走到较小节点。

sentences.en: Any other letter that is greater than and starts at it, you're going to go to the higher node.
sentences.zh: 任何其他大于它且以它开头的字母，你都会走到较大节点。

sentences.en: And then any other word that's building off of C is going to go to the equal node somehow.
sentences.zh: 然后任何其他基于 C 构建的单词都会以某种方式走到相等节点。

sentences.en: So like I understand all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我理解所有这些。

sentences.en: The only thing I don't understand is like if you've got like chapel, so a C-H, how do you indicate that?
sentences.zh: 我唯一不明白的是，比如如果你有 chapel，那么 C-H，你怎么表示它？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，对。

sentences.en: So I think this is it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为就是这样。

sentences.en: Anytime you take the non-equal node, if you take the low or the high node, you are not including that parent node that you came from.
sentences.zh: 任何时候你选择非相等节点，如果你选择较小或较大节点，你就不包括你来自的那个父节点。

sentences.en: So in the case of cup, you include the C because you're using the equal to, you include the U because you're going straight down as well.
sentences.zh: 所以在 cup 的例子中，你包括 C，因为你使用了相等，你也包括 U，因为你也是直接向下走。

sentences.en: But then when you get to the T, if you take the low node, which means you go to P, you leave out the T.
sentences.zh: 但当你到达 T 时，如果你选择较小节点，这意味着你走到 P，你就留下了 T。

sentences.en: Yeah, the TST is, I won't say infinitely more complex, but like definitely like one of the major differences between a TST and a dog is that a dog, when constructed,
sentences.zh: 是的，TST，我不会说它无限复杂，但绝对是 TST 和狗（dog）之间的主要区别之一是，狗在构建时，

sentences.en: only has one representation.
sentences.zh: 只有一种表示形式。

sentences.en: And when searching for a word, you're basically guaranteed to only search the number of characters in that word to see if it exists in that dictionary at moSt.
sentences.zh: 当搜索一个单词时，你基本上保证最多只搜索该单词中的字符数量，看看它是否存在于该字典中。

sentences.en: That's if you hit a match.
sentences.zh: 那是如果你匹配成功的话。

sentences.en: If the word you're searching for does not exist in the dictionary, at some point you're going to find out, oh, this word, you know, at the fourth letter,
sentences.zh: 如果你搜索的单词在字典中不存在，在某个点你会发现，哦，这个单词，你知道，在第四个字母处，

sentences.en: we don't have anywhere to go.
sentences.zh: 我们无处可去了。

sentences.en: This word doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这个词并不存在。

sentences.en: Whereas in this TST, depending on how it's constructed, you could search, I'm not sure what the bound is, but definitely more nodes than are in the word,
sentences.zh: 而在这种TST中，取决于它的构建方式，你可以进行搜索，我不确定具体的界限是多少，但肯定比单词里的节点要多，

sentences.en: the characters of the word that you're searching for.
sentences.zh: 也就是你正在搜索的单词里的字符。

sentences.en: But yeah, we'll say thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 总之，感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Hopefully this episode post-editing is less of a mess than it was while recording.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目剪辑后不会像录制时那么混乱。

sentences.en: I personally learned something as a co-host, as a listener, that's up in the air at this moment.
sentences.zh: 作为联合主持人和听众，我个人是否学到了东西，目前还不好说。

sentences.en: But yeah, thanks for listening and we'll catch everyone in the next episode, hopefully, unless if you just uninstalled this podcast from your podcast listening app.
sentences.zh: 总之，感谢收听，我们下期节目再见，希望如此，除非你已经把这个播客从你的收听应用里卸载了。

sentences.en: We'll see you guys next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次再见。
